title: Why I started this blog
excerpt: Notes on what I'm learning, the projects I'm building, and what it's actually like working as a frontend developer.
content:
I've wanted a place to write for a while now. Somewhere to put the code snippets, the bugs I chase down, the tools I keep reaching for, and the things I learn on the way.

Why bother writing?

Because writing is the fastest way to actually understand something. The moment you have to explain it, you find the parts you only thought you understood. It also leaves me a trail to come back to later.

What goes here?

- React, JavaScript, and the rest of the frontend toolbox
- Things I figure out while building projects
- Tools that genuinely earn their place
- Mistakes I make, so I stop repeating them

I wrote this post from my own admin panel — so adding a post, dropping in an image, and editing it later is all something I can do without touching the code.

title: Why I rebuilt my portfolio
excerpt: The old one was a list of projects. This one is an actual application — backend, database, and an admin panel.
content:
The old portfolio was simple: one page listing my projects.

So what was wrong with it?

Everything was hardcoded. To add a project I edited a file by hand and redeployed. No admin panel, no analytics, no way to change anything without a commit. It was a static page pretending to be a portfolio.

What changed?

There's a real backend behind the site now: admin authentication, project management, an inbox for messages, visit analytics, and now a blog. Adding a post means filling in a form.

What I learned:

1. Serverless deployment has its own logic. The filesystem is read-only and every lambda instance is isolated. Miss that and you get a strange bug that only shows up in production.

2. A test has to be able to fail. A test that can't catch a bug is worth nothing.

3. Keep it simple. The more moving parts, the more places it breaks.
